title: Swe senior domain cap theorem
question: Explain the CAP theorem and how you'd apply it to actually justify a design decision, not just recite the definitions.
idealAnswer:
States the three properties correctly: consistency (every read sees the most recent write), availability (every request gets a non-error response), partition tolerance (the system keeps working despite network partitions between nodes)

Correctly frames the real tradeoff: since network partitions will happen in any distributed system, partition tolerance isn't really optional, so the meaningful choice under a partition is between consistency and availability

Avoids the common oversimplification of treating CAP as a permanent, global three-way pick, a strong answer notes the choice can be made per-operation or per-service, not necessarily system-wide

Gives a concrete example of a system that favors availability over strict consistency (e.g. a shopping cart that stays usable during a partition, resolving conflicts later) versus one that must favor consistency (e.g. a financial ledger that would rather reject a request than risk an incorrect balance)

Connects it to a practical implication like eventual consistency, and can explain what 'eventual' actually commits to (the system will converge, but reads may be stale until it does)
